deckTitle: Medicine Madness: The Waiting Room Anarchy

cards.power: Eliminate one non-corporate player from the board.
cards.lore: A 1910 document that systematically replaced diverse healing traditions with petrochemical pipelines.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the report. Immediate saboteur clarity — wipe the natural healers.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gritty political cartoon. Subject: suited badger bulldozing a herb garden. Mood: corporate triumphant.

cards.power: Pay 5 coins to rewrite the rulebook in your favor.
cards.lore: Rockefeller grants ensuring only the academics teaching the pill-pushing curriculum survive the winter.
cards.gradeReason: Octopus with a green cross is sharp — role clicks on second beat, not first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial cartoon. Subject: octopus in top hat clutching medical textbooks and money bags. Mood: benevolent menace.

cards.power: Convert 3 organic resources into 1 synthetic, patentable asset.
cards.lore: Standardized, rigorously sterile, and perfectly calibrated to prescribe the funder's products.
cards.gradeReason: Power is clever but 'German University Model' is a concept, not a role to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical academic. Subject: robot bear in lab coat manufacturing pills from vegetables. Mood: sterile efficiency.

cards.power: Target loses all active nature-based healing buffs.
cards.lore: No corporate grant, no state license. The botanical traditions fade to black.
cards.gradeReason: You are the shutdown notice. Strip the healers. Simple, merciless, instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic satire. Subject: padlocked herbalist school sign in rain, weeds overtaking the door. Mood: erasure.

cards.power: Target player discards their hand and stops paying you rent.
cards.lore: A catastrophic strategic error for any pharmaceutical portfolio. The cured patient does not return.
cards.gradeReason: The lore IS the card. 'The cured patient does not return' lands like a verdict.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor noir. Subject: healthy stag walking away from a pharma tower, stock ticker crashing. Mood: devastating irony.

cards.power: Generate 1 coin every turn for the rest of the game.
cards.lore: The holy grail: daily medication, indefinitely, with cascading side effects requiring further medication.
cards.gradeReason: 'The holy grail: daily medication, indefinitely' — you are the subscription model.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical cartoon. Subject: sheep on hamster wheel inside a pharma vault, drip IV attached. Mood: profitable despair.

cards.power: Move the goalposts. Target player must re-roll healthy stats until they trigger a condition.
cards.lore: Lowering the threshold of healthy until the entire population requires a daily pill.
cards.gradeReason: 'Move the goalposts' is an immediately playable instruction. Everyone gets this instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic satire. Subject: committee of owls sliding a SICKNESS banner over a healthy patient. Mood: predatory officiousness.

cards.power: Hide 3 cards face-down; opponents cannot read them until they trigger.
cards.lore: Eleven experts defining the disease, who just happen to be funded by the manufacturer of the cure.
cards.gradeReason: Hide cards, manufacture science — every player immediately knows this conspiracy move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: smoky boardroom cartoon. Subject: masked raccoons at a table stamping documents APPROVED. Mood: secretive legitimacy.

cards.power: [partially obscured] Believed safe for 2 years, banned in 1961 after birth defects in 10,000+ children.
cards.lore: Believed safe for 2 years, banned in 1961 after birth defects in 10,000+ children. Some scandals survive.
cards.gradeReason: Historical name anchors immediately — power text resolution made mechanics unclear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark editorial. Subject: cheerful drug bottle with skull motif, approval stamp cracking. Mood: delayed catastrophe.

cards.power: Design the experiment to get the answer you need.
cards.lore: Designing the experiment to get the answer you need is still called 'science.'
cards.gradeReason: Pig-in-lab-coat image lands the satire — but needs one beat to clock the joke.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: mad scientist cartoon. Subject: pig in lab coat with clipboard, surrounded by compliant lab rats. Mood: rigged certainty.

cards.power: HALT. Stall approval by asking for data on the data. The US babies survived because you existed.
cards.lore: FDA bureaucrat who single-handedly prevented US thalidomide approval by demanding evidence from the evidence.
cards.gradeReason: HALT. One word, one hero, one instant role. Purest G1 in the sequence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: heroic watercolor. Subject: determined wolf in government blazer holding up a HALT sign against a flood of pills. Mood: lone defiance.

cards.power: [partially obscured] Industry-funded studies do their own thing.
cards.lore: Industry-funded studies do their own thing. Peer review is a journal subscription service.
cards.gradeReason: Requires science literacy but the satire is sharp for any educated table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: academic satire. Subject: two scientists with contradictory charts, both labeled PEER REVIEWED. Mood: epistemic chaos.

cards.power: Drain 1 health from all players per turn by hiding your wealth.
cards.lore: 500,000+ dead, trillions of profit, and a settlement requiring barely any accountability. No budget.
cards.gradeReason: '500,000+ dead, trillions of profit' — you are the system. Brutal, immediate, undeniable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark pyramid satire. Subject: opioid pill pyramid built on tombstones with cash raining down. Mood: monumental rot.

cards.power: Reposition target player into a pain-rating machine.
cards.lore: A brilliant, lethal, industry-funded campaign to make opioids the gold standard of pain management.
cards.gradeReason: You ARE the campaign. Role is crisp — turn pain into a product mandate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: retro medical poster parody. Subject: smiley face pain scale morphing into a pill dispenser. Mood: clinical cheerfulness.

cards.power: Draft a sympathetic press front from a coalition of patient groups.
cards.lore: A grassroots patient movement entirely produced by Purdue Pharma. No grass. No roots.
cards.gradeReason: Lore closer ('No grass. No roots.') is excellent — but 'advocacy front' needs a moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: astroturf satire. Subject: pharma wolf in patient clothing holding a homemade protest sign. Mood: performed sincerity.

cards.power: Escape game-over by paying exactly 10% of your total haul in fines.
cards.lore: Pay a billion in fines, keep ten billion in profits, admitting absolutely no wrongdoing.
cards.gradeReason: 10% fine mechanic is the whole story. Instant corporate get-out-of-jail role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: courtroom cartoon. Subject: fat cat signing a tiny check labeled 1/10th while bags of cash exit stage right. Mood: legal farce.

cards.power: [partially obscured] Removed from market after causing 30-60K heart attacks.
cards.lore: Removed from market after causing 30,000-60,000 heart attacks. A business unit, not a disaster.
cards.gradeReason: Name lands hard post-2004 but requires cultural memory — strong for the target demo.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: product recall parody. Subject: cheerful pill mascot with warning label reading may cause permanent stoppage. Mood: corporate PR disaster.

cards.power: Profits > Corpses. OK.
cards.lore: The internal memo you were never supposed to see. A known risk, a known outcome, a known decision.
cards.gradeReason: 'Profits > Corpses OK!' — three words, instant villain role, zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: boardroom dark comedy. Subject: executives at whiteboard with the equation Profits > Corpses, nodding. Mood: banal evil.

cards.power: Create a simplified narrative moat that makes it scientifically difficult to question the treatment.
cards.lore: A simplified, unverified, and perfectly marketable story that colonized medical schools and consumer culture for forty years.
cards.gradeReason: The castle-with-moat image is perfect — but 'serotonin hypothesis' is jargon for some tables.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fantasy science parody. Subject: fairy-tale castle labeled DEPRESSION = CHEMICAL IMBALANCE surrounded by a moat of pills. Mood: captivating fiction.

cards.power: Report a simplified biological story to a willing audience. Shape perception, not data.
cards.lore: Reporting a simplified biological story to a willing audience. The audience asked for this. We provided it.
cards.gradeReason: Clear satirical frame but slightly generic — lacks a specific hook.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ad-agency satire. Subject: fox presenter pointing at a colorful brain scan labeled PROOF before a cheering crowd. Mood: manufactured consensus.

cards.power: Play a card bypassing all standard research safety checks. Emergency conditions apply.
cards.lore: [partially obscured — references emergency bypassing of standard research protocols]
cards.gradeReason: Deliberately charged — strong provocateur card, but complexity needs table literacy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: biotech thriller. Subject: glowing syringe launching from a rocket labeled EMERGENCY, skipping safety checkpoints. Mood: accelerated urgency.

cards.power: Button off ongoing regulatory review outside normal timeline. Emergency conditions apply.
cards.lore: The rules exist. The emergency pauses them. The emergency never quite ends.
cards.gradeReason: Recognizable post-2020 — clear role but dense text obscured mechanics at this resolution.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic emergency. Subject: rhinoceros rubber-stamping APPROVED at speed, documents scattered. Mood: approved chaos.

cards.power: Delay the effects of an opponent's outcome unless they pay to open it. Winning is deferred.
cards.lore: Releasing the clinical trial data only after everyone who analyzed it has died.
cards.gradeReason: The lore is one of the darkest in the corpus. Immediately playable saboteur move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark archive satire. Subject: vault labeled 2096 ONLY with skeletons of scientists outside. Mood: bureaucratic eternity.

cards.power: Bury all damage tokens done this turn. Nothing happened.
cards.lore: If someone persists in reporting, the suppressed count accumulates until forced disclosure.
cards.gradeReason: 'Nothing happened.' is the full brief. Two words, pure conspirator mechanics.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cover-up cartoon. Subject: corporate ostrich burying a stack of medical reports in sand. Mood: cheerful erasure.

cards.power: Rotate between public defense and private profit with the same credentials.
cards.lore: The revolving door between regulator and regulated. Same gecko, different badge.
cards.gradeReason: Revolving door concept is clear — but 'gecko' as mascot needs a beat to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political cartoon. Subject: chameleon in FDA uniform on one side, pharma exec suit on the other, spinning through a door. Mood: seamless corruption.

cards.power: The regulator's operational budget depends entirely on approving the one it's supposed to review.
cards.lore: A regulatory agency funded by the industry it regulates. The umpire is on the payroll.
cards.gradeReason: PDUFA acronym is a table-stopper. Lore explains it but the name requires a handout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: financial satire. Subject: referee accepting an envelope from a player mid-game while holding a rulebook. Mood: institutional capture.

cards.power: Your vote counts. Unless you are outnumbered by those with industry ties. You are outnumbered.
cards.lore: Independent experts making critical recommendations, of whom the majority hold undisclosed industry relationships.
cards.gradeReason: The structure is universally recognizable — the corruption satire lands cleanly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: committee room satire. Subject: table of cats voting while one honest rabbit raises its hand alone. Mood: rigged deliberation.

cards.power: Pay 5 coins to privately dictate the next major card drawn from the deck.
cards.lore: Ensuring global health priorities mirror your investment portfolio. Voluntary. Of course.
cards.gradeReason: Strong geopolitical satire but abstract for tables without WHO context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: global governance satire. Subject: billionaire dropping a coin in a WHO DONATION slot, global health agenda reshuffling. Mood: philanthropic control.

cards.power: Reveal the top 3 cards of the deck, but your next turn is spent defending your credibility.
cards.lore: The credibility of a man who claimed to cure cancer with frequencies is destroyed by the cure working.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is devastating — but Rife is niche knowledge. Strong for informed tables.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: forgotten genius satire. Subject: lone scientist with frequency equipment, his lab window bricked up behind him. Mood: historical erasure.

cards.power: Destroy one opponent's item on the board permanently.
cards.lore: The credibility of lab equipment that you cannot destroy is instead destroyed by fire.
cards.gradeReason: Burn the lab. Instant, archetypal conspiracy move. Everyone plays this without hesitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir arson cartoon. Subject: well-dressed wolf watching a research lab burn at midnight, hands in pockets. Mood: convenient catastrophe.

cards.power: Use natural resources to heal; opponents can label your methods unscientific without evidence.
cards.lore: Healed terminal patients with organic diets, became an obstacle, was removed. Because you can't patent a carrot.
cards.gradeReason: 'You can't patent a carrot' is a knockout line — but Gerson is niche for some tables.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: folk healer satire. Subject: wise rabbit with carrot-based treatment, FDA WANTED poster behind him. Mood: persecuted virtue.

cards.power: Provides immense healing but cannot be monetized or traded. WORTHLESS.
cards.lore: Authentically effective. Completely unacceptable. Cannot generate a recurring revenue stream. WORTHLESS.
cards.gradeReason: WORTHLESS stamp + the anti-logic is peak Kayfabizarro. Instant table activation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: satirical product label. Subject: glowing carrot stamped WORTHLESS in red ink, surrounded by rejected patent forms. Mood: capitalist absurdity.

cards.power: Access healing items for 3 consecutive turns without spending coins.
cards.lore: A herbal cancer treatment practitioner with clinical successes. Banned anyway. The clinic moved to Tijuana.
cards.gradeReason: The Tijuana connection makes the next card land harder — but Hoxsey needs intro.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: folk medicine poster. Subject: cowboy horse with herb bundles, FDA CLOSED notice being nailed to his door. Mood: defiant displacement.

cards.power: Evade regulatory shutdown by operating outside jurisdiction. Continue from the border.
cards.lore: Removed from US jurisdiction. Continues from Mexico, outside the reach of the FDA.
cards.gradeReason: Instantly evocative — you know exactly why you're in Tijuana. Zero explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: border noir. Subject: medical clinic sign glowing just south of a fence line, patients crossing to reach it. Mood: exiled legitimacy.

cards.power: A medication with decades of safety data and a Nobel Prize. Opponents are still powerless against this card.
cards.lore: Made suddenly controversial for political, not medical, reasons. The Nobel Prize did not help.
cards.gradeReason: Post-2020 this name is an instant table-activator. Maximum polarization. Ideal Kayfabizarro.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political satire. Subject: Nobel Prize medal labeled IVERMECTIN with a big red X stamped over it by a news logo. Mood: weaponized controversy.

cards.power: Remove 1 card from the game entirely. It cannot be called back by any event.
cards.lore: Before a pandemic, cards from every alternative category are relabeled until the full-game crisis resolves.
cards.gradeReason: Clear mechanics — slightly abstract framing but reads to anyone who lived through 2020.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: wartime censorship. Subject: shelves of medical treatments with one slot dramatically empty, RESTRICTED tape across it. Mood: selective emergency.

cards.power: Repeat your last 10-chip action for free if target player agrees it was voluntary.
cards.lore: Selected for pre-existing conviction. Amplifies a pre-approved, industry-preferred narrative.
cards.gradeReason: 'SAFE AND EFFECTIVE!' — this is a top-10 card name in the entire corpus. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medical propaganda parody. Subject: parrot in lab coat on a perch, SAFE AND EFFECTIVE banner looping on a screen behind it. Mood: automated endorsement.

cards.power: Force all players to parrot your last action as if they attended the sponsored training.
cards.lore: The credentialed body of practitioners brought together for a branded continuing medical education conference.
cards.gradeReason: The starling murmuration metaphor is brilliant — but CME requires medical context to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: flock satire. Subject: hundreds of identical bird-doctors all facing the same pharma-branded screen. Mood: credentialed conformity.

cards.power: Automate disease definition rotation; deploy industry-branded public awareness campaign.
cards.lore: A publicly facing bird that lays its eggs in public health nests. The host raises the chick.
cards.gradeReason: Cuckoo-as-astroturf is clever — but mechanism slightly dense at table speed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: nature doc parody. Subject: cuckoo bird in a public health nest, smaller birds feeding it awareness campaign materials. Mood: parasitic goodwill.

cards.power: Reveal 1 full disclosure on an opponent's play card; cancel one undisclosed conflict of interest.
cards.lore: The sole individual who checks the disclosures. Powerful, but outnumbered by those who don't.
cards.gradeReason: Good hero card but 'footnote reader' is a quiet role — works at a smart table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: detective satire. Subject: hedgehog with magnifying glass reading the fine print of a giant medical paper. Mood: determined futility.

cards.power: Design the dice that, when rolled, are guaranteed to succeed. Call it methodology.
cards.lore: Build the trial around a proven placebo instead of the active drug. Guarantee a win. Publish anyway.
cards.gradeReason: Technical but perfect for medical or academic tables — mechanics are sharp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: rigged science satire. Subject: architect cat designing a trial where all paths lead to EFFICACY. Mood: engineered certainty.

cards.power: Provide alternative healing. Do not exceed 2x a clinical trial claim or face license revocation.
cards.lore: The credibility-testing zone in the therapeutic market. Operate at the margin or be removed from it.
cards.gradeReason: Clear regulatory satire on the licensing threat — works well but is reactive rather than active.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tightrope satire. Subject: naturopath hedgehog balancing between healing and a REVOKED LICENCE sign. Mood: constrained legitimacy.

cards.power: Revoke any player's ability to use healing cards for 2 full turns.
cards.lore: A gatekeeper entity created by a trade group to define who gets to practice. Gatekeeping as a service.
cards.gradeReason: Clear but generic — the mechanic is solid, the name doesn't pop.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: bureaucratic authority. Subject: pompous bear tribunal stamping REVOKED on a medical license. Mood: institutional power trip.

cards.power: Activate your full bureaucracy to any corporate or regulatory board position simultaneously.
cards.lore: The institutional pipeline that ensures every regulatory body has the right people in the right chairs.
cards.gradeReason: 'Migratory Bureaucrat Swarm' is a great name — power text slightly abstract on first read.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: migration parody. Subject: suited locusts swarming between FDA, WHO, and pharma offices in one motion. Mood: systemic occupation.

cards.power: Force an opponent to completely skip their turn due to administrative delay.
cards.lore: A system best designed to prevent a patient from ever asking the questions that count.
cards.gradeReason: Everyone has lived this. The cover image. Zero explanation needed. Universal G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chaotic animal waiting room. Subject: overcrowded clinic, clock showing 4 hours, patients resigned. Mood: systemic exhaustion.

cards.power: Play a card without reading it. Write a script. Get them out.
cards.lore: The appointment-level decision. The prescription was ready before the consultation began.
cards.gradeReason: 'Write a script, get them out' — devastating and universal. Pure performative role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medical satire. Subject: dog doctor glancing at clipboard for 2 seconds before handing a prescription. Mood: efficient dismissal.

cards.power: [partially obscured] Side effects listed cheerfully in the final two seconds.
cards.lore: [partially obscured] Gets the patient pre-sold on the product before the appointment.
cards.gradeReason: RECALLED stamp is a sharp visual — power text resolution too muddy for full read.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: DTC pharma ad parody. Subject: happy cartoon animal holding pills, RECALLED stamped across the poster. Mood: belated honesty.

cards.power: Attach to a buffed roll. It takes 1 damage per turn for every roll it's currently buffing until it expires.
cards.lore: A regulatory mechanism longer than the medication's clinical justification, read by no one.
cards.gradeReason: Clever cascading damage mechanic — requires one explanation but then plays cleanly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: absurdist legal satire. Subject: turtle unrolling an impossibly long side-effects scroll across the table. Mood: mandatory incomprehension.

cards.power: Break any rule, pay 2 coins, keep all other profits. The fine is a cost of doing business.
cards.lore: A single percent of the victim pool weighted against the total haul. This is not a deterrent. This is a tariff.
cards.gradeReason: 'The fine is a cost of doing business' — instant executive role, zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: scales-of-justice satire. Subject: scales tipped by a tiny fine versus a mountain of profit, both labeled RESOLVED. Mood: legal farce.

cards.power: Convert a dead-end healing loop into a permanent, repeating disease management protocol.
cards.lore: Efficacy remains a dead end. Management is a recurring, perfectly held revenue stream.
cards.gradeReason: The distinction is razor-sharp — requires one beat to parse but lands perfectly after.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: business model satire. Subject: two arrows — CURE pointing to a cliff, MANAGE pointing to an infinite loop. Mood: engineered dependency.

cards.power: Make all of your cards entirely immune to regulatory attacks for 2 turns.
cards.lore: A blank license provided by a trade group you funded, to certify the practices you defined.
cards.gradeReason: Clean mechanic — but name is the blandest in the deck. Does the heavy lifting quietly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: credentialism satire. Subject: fox holding a gold-seal certificate reading DEFINITELY LEGITIMATE. Mood: self-certified authority.

cards.power: Bury an opponent's most powerful healing card. It cannot be retrieved this game.
cards.lore: The competitor's strongest asset, disappeared through regulatory, legal, or financial means. Nothing personal.
cards.gradeReason: Strong but slightly echoes The Suppressed Adverse Event — both suppress cards dilute each other.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate burial. Subject: briefcase labeled ALTERNATIVE dropped into a filing void labeled SUPPRESSED. Mood: clean elimination.

cards.power: [partially obscured — references corporate raid and health penalties]
cards.lore: [partially obscured — references corporate failure to deliver on its own system]
cards.gradeReason: Muddy power text, unclear role — what does a player actually DO as this card?
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pharmacy satire. Subject: empty prescription bottle on a shelf, OUT OF STOCK sign behind a harried pharmacist. Mood: systemic abandonment.

cards.power: Reveal all face-down cards on the board and immediately negate their loops.
cards.lore: Exists. Is occasionally allowed to find out things. The highest level of evidence. Rarely convenient.
cards.gradeReason: The hero card. 'Reveal all, negate their loops' — clean, powerful, instant justice move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sunlight-through-clouds satire. Subject: academic crow holding up a meta-analysis, corporate face-down cards flipping over in shock. Mood: inconvenient truth.

cards.power: Create a card where corporate players have absolutely no effect. You are the deck. Build it.
cards.lore: A hand-drawn deck beyond the reach of the system. This is it. You're holding it.
cards.gradeReason: The meta-card. You ARE the sketchbook. Self-aware closer with maximum emotional punch.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: meta-satirical. Subject: rabbit hand-drawing a card of itself drawing a card. Mood: recursive resistance.

cards.cardName: The System Is Running on Time
cards.power: The game ends. The player with the most Conspira chips is immune to any future consequence.
cards.lore: Everything is working as designed. The system is on time. I am leaving.
cards.gradeReason: Devastating closer — but 'the game ends' is a lot for a single card to carry mid-session.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: clockwork dystopia. Subject: rabbit in a suit walking away from a perfectly functioning corrupt machine, clock ticking. Mood: resigned lucidity.

verdict: The Saboteur Sketchbook is the most structurally ambitious deck in the corpus — 14 thematic sequences flowing from the 1910 Flexner Report through pandemic-era suppression to FrizzleBob's personal exit. The organizational architecture alone earns it a special mention: Founding Architecture → Subscription Model → Five Scandal Sequences → The Eliminated → The Fauna → Clinical Encounter → System's Arsenal → Exit Strategy is a complete documentary in card form. Named strength: the Sickness Subscription Model sequence (cards 5-8) is perfect — 'A cured patient is a catastrophic loss of recurring revenue' belongs in the all-time Kayfabizarro vault. Named weakness: power text on several back-half pages runs small and was partially illegible at table resolution — PDUFA, The Unfilled Prescription, and the mRNA cards lose clarity. Table-ready YES — with a font-size audit on power text recommended.
blurb: For anyone who's ever been told their question was dangerous. The Saboteur Sketchbook deals the full history of pharmaceutical monopoly as a 56-card game — and ends with the one card they cannot regulate.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: MEDICINE MADNESS: THE WAITING ROOM ANARCHY – Play the Full History of Captured Medicine (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

When did asking what is actually in the pill become the dangerous part?

Run the numbers the way the industry runs them. A molecule you can patent earns back a billion-dollar trial. A cheap vegetable, an old generic, a fasting protocol earns nobody anything, so it never gets the trial, so it never gets the evidence, so it stays "unproven" forever by design. That is not a gap in the science. That is the business model working exactly as built. The key opinion leader gets flown to the conference, the inconvenient result gets filed under acceptable business risk, and the person who actually recovered becomes a number nobody is paid to publish.

Medicine Madness deals that machine as a game you run with your own hands. This is Social Story Wrestling for the waiting room: 56 cut-and-play cards and fourteen scandals deep, a roster you perform out loud until the table decides whether the cover story holds or gets exposed mid-sentence.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Medicine Madness Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Key Opinion Leader Parrot, the expert who repeats whatever the last grant told him, The Unpatentable Vegetable, the cure with no margin and therefore no trial, and The Cured Patient, the outcome the system has no billing code for.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no medical degree, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one law that every card can claim anything, as long as you can sell it before the room calls the work.
- The 14-Scandal Investigation: the deck runs as one continuous case, fourteen named chapters deep, from the early capture of the field to the exit strategy, so you watch organized medicine get bought one chapter at a time. It ends on Frances Oldham Kelsey, the regulator who looked at the data and said no, the one card they could never quite regulate.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
You are not buying a static PDF. You are buying into the Dark Journalism cycle. Every future chapter, every new scandal folded into this investigation, every sibling deck in the series lands in your library as a free update. The file grows as the case does.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I trained in medicine, and I have watched good questions get relabeled as dangerous ones. This deck hands the whole captured history back to you as a toy you are allowed to break. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Read it, print it, run the racket yourself at the kitchen table until you can spot the move in the wild. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next comic cards and sharper mechanics.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
They can patent the molecule. They can never patent the question.
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
